title.en: STONEWORK — Semantic Threat Ontology and Research Framework

description.undefined: A semantic threat ontology and research framework that serves as the ground-truth model for cyber threat intelligence in the CyberTerrain ecosystem. It provides an extensible foundation for modeling cyber threat intelligence concepts, objects, relationships, workflows, and knowledge, and aligns with established CTI framework ontologies — including STONES (STIX 2.1), ATT&CK, CAPEC, CWE, CVE, and CPE — as authoritative reference vocabularies rather than ontologies it imports and extends.

title.value: STONEWORK — Semantic Threat Ontology and Research Framework

definition.value: An abstract software, hardware, or firmware product line identified by vendor and product name, independent of any specific version or release. Represents the collection of all versioned releases built under that product identity.

scopeNote.value: stonework:Product does not carry version, update, edition, or other release-specific attributes. Those belong on stonework:VersionedProduct. The two classes are disjoint.

comment.en: Instances of stonework:Product represent product families or lines (e.g. 'Apache Log4j', 'Windows 10'). Specific releases are modeled as stonework:VersionedProduct individuals related via stonework:versionOf. CPE entries with wildcard version components map to stonework:Product; entries with concrete versions map to stonework:VersionedProduct.

definition.value: A telephone number used to contact or identify an Agent. Used for attribution, OSINT pivoting, and identity clustering.
A structured, machine-readable rule designed to detect malicious or suspicious activity, techniques, or indicators. It may be signature-based, behavioral, correlation-based, or analytic.

scopeNote.value: Encompasses pattern-matching signatures (YARA, Snort, Suricata), behavioral rules (Sigma), SIEM correlation logic, and analytic detections. Signature is a subclass for content-centric, indicator-matching rules.

definition.value: A structured artifact produced by an intelligence or analytical process, intended to convey findings, assessments, observations, or sourcing context to support decision-making.

scopeNote.value: The intelligence product hierarchy covers the outputs of the intelligence lifecycle: Reports, Assessments, Sightings, Notes, and Provenance records. Distinguished from stonework:DigitalArtifact (raw observable technical data) and stonework:Behavior (plan specifications and TTP patterns). Intelligence products are the result of human or automated analytical work applied to raw data — they carry judgment, context, and traceability that raw artifacts do not.

definition.value: A high-level defensive objective that groups related countermeasure techniques by the protection goal they serve.

scopeNote.value: Aligns with MITRE D3FEND defensive tactics (e.g. Harden, Detect, Isolate, Evict, Restore). Individuals are typically drawn from D3FEND or similar defensive frameworks via the framework mapping layer.

definition.value: A high-level adversary objective that groups related attack techniques by the goal they serve during an intrusion or operation.

scopeNote.value: Aligns with MITRE ATT&CK tactics (e.g. Initial Access, Execution, Lateral Movement) and D3FEND OffensiveTactic. Individuals are typically drawn from ATT&CK or similar offensive frameworks via the STONES or framework mapping layers.

definition.value: A string identifier transmitted by a client application in HTTP requests declaring the software, version, and platform making the request. Used for fingerprinting clients, identifying malware C2 beaconing patterns, and clustering infrastructure by shared tooling.

scopeNote.value: User-agent strings are observable in network traffic, proxy logs, and web server logs. Distinctive or spoofed user-agent values are commonly used as indicators in threat intelligence. Distinct from stonework:UserAccount (an identity credential) — a UserAgent describes software behavior, not a user identity.

definition.value: A significant adverse event or series of related events that has caused, or has the potential to cause, harm to an organization’s operations, assets, or people.

scopeNote.value: Distinguished from stonework:Event (a raw, unassessed occurrence) by the presence of human or automated triage declaring significance and adversity. An Incident may aggregate multiple Events, involve one or more Campaigns, and trigger Investigation and Playbook execution.

definition.value: Represents systems, software services, or any group of resources used to conduct cyber operations. Infrastructure is used by threat actors and intrusion sets both offensively and defensively.
Represents a single IP address (IPv4 or IPv6).

A type of flaw, fault, or design condition in software, hardware, or system architecture that can enable vulnerabilities, reduce security assurance, or increase the likelihood of exploitable behavior.

scopeNote.value: This class provides a semantic representation of weakness types defined in the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE). It supports hierarchical relationships, abstraction levels, and mappings to related attack patterns, vulnerabilities, and security controls.

comment.undefined: Instances of stonework:Weakness may represent base weaknesses, variant weaknesses, or compound weaknesses. CWE identifiers (e.g., "CWE‑79") SHOULD be modeled using explicit properties rather than encoded in the class IRI. Descriptions and extended details SHOULD be referenced via citations rather than reproduced verbatim.

definition.value: A formal, machine-readable inventory of VersionedProduct components that constitute a software artifact or system, expressed in a standard format such as CycloneDX or SPDX.

scopeNote.value: Instances of stonework:SoftwareBillOfMaterials correspond to SBOM documents. Component membership is expressed via stonework:hasBomEntry. Format metadata (CycloneDX, SPDX, etc.) SHOULD be carried as datatype properties.

comment.en: An SBOM asserts that specific VersionedProduct instances are components of a containing artifact. The containing artifact may itself be a VersionedProduct related to this SBOM via stonework:hasBomEntry.

definition.value: A single, identifiable human actor with the capability and intent to conduct adversarial cyber activities.

scopeNote.value: Covers individual hackers, insiders, contractors, and other identified persons. Relevant for law enforcement and prosecution contexts where attribution to a specific individual — rather than a group — is required. Distinguished from stonework:ThreatActorGroup, which represents a collective or organization.

definition.value: A systematic Process of inquiry, evidence collection, analysis, hypothesis testing, and conclusion to understand, attribute, or resolve security incidents, threats, anomalies, or other matters of interest.

scopeNote.value: Includes digital forensics, threat hunting, root cause analysis, and incident investigations. Links to Sightings, Evidence (via categorizedBy), Sensors, and produces Findings or updated Assessments.

definition.value: A prescribed offensive method used by an adversary to achieve a specific tactical objective within a target environment.

scopeNote.value: Aligns with MITRE ATT&CK techniques and D3FEND OffensiveTechnique. Not a subclass of stones:AttackPattern — attack patterns (e.g. CAPEC) are abstract descriptions of attack classes, whereas AttackTechnique is an operationalized plan for execution. Framework-specific subclasses (e.g. attack:Technique) provide the concrete individuals.

definition.value: Any collection of Persons, Organizations, or other Groups that share a common purpose or identity but do not necessarily have formal legal structure.

scopeNote.value: Used for informal collectives, communities, ad-hoc teams, criminal syndicates, or loose alliances. More general than Organization. Can contain other Groups or Organizations.

definition.value: A network-accessible service or endpoint provided by infrastructure, such as HTTP, DNS, or SSH servers.
A systematic examination of a cyber entity, artifact, or event that produces structured findings about its nature, behavior, or properties.

scopeNote.value: Sibling to stonework:Assessment under IntelligenceProduct. Where Assessment answers 'how bad/likely/risky?', Analysis answers 'what is it and what does it do?' Superclass for domain-specific analyses such as MalwareAnalysis. Aligns with STIX MalwareAnalysis SDO at the subclass level.

definition.value: A plan specification describing how a threat could materialize against specific assets or missions — incorporating adversary intent, capability, opportunity, preconditions, attack path, and expected consequences.

scopeNote.value: A ThreatScenario is prescriptive and forward-looking: it specifies a potential sequence of adversary behaviors and environmental conditions rather than recording observed events. Used to guide defensive planning, risk assessment, and Playbook development. Distinct from stonework:Incident (an observed occurrence) and stonework:Threat (an abstract source of harm). Aligns with prov:Plan and P-Plan scenario specifications.

definition.value: A Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) block used to represent an IP network range.
A structured record of findings from static or dynamic analysis performed on a malware specimen or family, including the tool used, analysis configuration, and verdict.

scopeNote.value: Captures the output of a single analysis run: antivirus scan, sandbox execution, reverse-engineering session, etc. Key properties include the analysis product and version, the result verdict (malicious/suspicious/benign/unknown), and references to SCOs observed during analysis. Corresponds to STIX 2.1 MalwareAnalysis SDO.

definition.value: A digital representation or persona of an Agent, inferred from one or more identifiers (email, phone, account, etc.). It may or may not be attributed to a known real-world Agent.

scopeNote.value: Useful when you observe identifiers without confirmed attribution. Can aggregate multiple Identifiers and later be linked to a real-worldAgent.

definition.value: Any concept, object, or resource that exists or operates within a cyber or sociotechnical domain.

scopeNote.value: One of two root classes in STONEWORK. Groups all persistent entities — Agents, Infrastructure, DigitalArtifacts, Behaviors, IntelligenceProducts, SecurityConditions, RiskFactors, Countermeasures, and related classes. Aligns with BFO Continuant. The sibling root class CyberActivity covers happenings (Campaigns, Incidents, Operations, etc.).

definition.value: A function, capacity, or part played by an entity in a specific context, relationship, or operation.

scopeNote.value: Roles are typically more stable and relational than Categories. An entity can play multiple Roles. Aligns with patterns in BFO, CCO, and D3FEND (e.g., functional roles of infrastructure or actors).

definition.value: A grouping of adversary behaviours and resources with a common objective pursued over a period of time. Campaigns may be attributed to ThreatActors and may evolve from a CyberActivityCluster as attribution and objectives become established.
Any discrete digital object or content entity that can be observed, transmitted, stored, or acted upon in a cyber environment.

scopeNote.value: Includes files, hashes, malware samples, network traffic captures, and other content-bearing items. Aligns with D3FEND DigitalArtifact concepts.

definition.value: The estimated probability, plausibility, or frequency with which a threat could be realized and lead to a compromise under specified conditions.

scopeNote.value: Likelihood reflects the chance that a compromise will occur, considering adversary capability, intent, opportunity, preconditions, and environmental factors. Likelihood values may be qualitative, ordinal, or quantitative.

comment.undefined: Instances of stonework:Likelihood may incorporate assumptions, uncertainty, adversary behavior, historical frequency, or environmental conditions. Likelihood SHOULD be represented using explicit properties rather than encoded in class IRIs or labels.

definition.value: A high‑level objective or strategic goal that groups related techniques by the purpose they serve during an operation.

scopeNote.value: Superclass for OffensiveTactic and DefensiveTactic. Tactics represent the strategic intent behind behavior — gaining initial access, exfiltrating data, or hardening a system. They serve as conceptual categories for techniques.

comment.undefined: Instances of stonework:Tactic SHOULD correspond to high‑level adversary goals. Techniques are typically modeled as children or members of a tactic.

definition.value: An atomic, observable occurrence in a system, network, or environment that has potential security relevance but has not yet been assessed or declared as an Incident.

scopeNote.value: Represents the pre-triage state — a raw log entry, alert, or sensor observation. Distinguished from Incident by the absence of human or automated assessment declaring it significant and adverse. Useful for SIEM, log-based, and threat hunting use cases.

definition.value: A pattern of actions or methods characteristic of an entity, particularly adversaries.

scopeNote.value: Groups TTP-related classes: Tactic, Technique (and subclasses), and Procedure. In BFO terms, Behaviors are GenericallyDependentContinuants — specifications or patterns describing how actions are carried out. The execution of a Technique is a CyberActivity; the Technique itself is a Behavior. Aligns with IAO PlanSpecification.

definition.value: A discrete unit of data stored on a filesystem, identified by name, path, and cryptographic hash. Includes executable binaries, scripts, documents, archives, and other file types relevant to cyber threat analysis.

scopeNote.value: Linked to hash values via stonework:hasHash. A MalwareSample may be associated with its File representation. Framework-specific extensions (PE headers, NTFS streams, archive contents) are modeled at the framework layer.

definition.value: A flaw or weakness in software, hardware, firmware, or system architecture that can be exploited by a threat actor to compromise confidentiality, integrity, or availability.

scopeNote.value: Represents specific exploitable instances (e.g., CVE-identified vulnerabilities) rather than weakness classes — those are modeled as stonework:Weakness. A Vulnerability is linked to its root Weakness via stonework:hasWeakness, to affected products via stonework:affected, to its fix via stonework:fixedInProduct, and to exploiting malware or actors via stonework:exploits. Aligns with D3FEND Vulnerability and NVD CVE.

definition.value: A collective, organization, or coordinated set of individuals operating with common intent to conduct adversarial cyber activities.

scopeNote.value: Covers nation-state units, cybercriminal organizations, hacktivist collectives, and other named adversary groups (e.g., APT29, Lazarus Group). MITRE ATT&CK serializes these as STIX intrusion-set objects; in STONEWORK they are correctly typed as ThreatActorGroup — an adversary entity rather than an activity cluster. Distinguished from stonework:ThreatActorIndividual, which represents a single human actor, and from stonework:CyberActivityCluster, which is the attributed set of activity linked to the group.

definition.value: Legitimate software that can be used offensively by threat actors or defensively by security practitioners. Distinguishable from malware by being designed for benign or dual-use purposes rather than being inherently malicious.

scopeNote.value: Includes commercial penetration testing tools, remote administration utilities, and living-off-the-land binaries (LOLBins) repurposed by adversaries, as well as defender-operated tools such as scanners, EDR agents, and forensic utilities. Corresponds to STIX 2.1 Tool SDO.

definition.value: A structured data source that provides indicators, intelligence, or enrichment data on a regular or continuous basis.

scopeNote.value: Examples: URLHaus, AlienVault OTX, Abuse.ch, commercial threat feeds, etc.

definition.value: A computing system, device, or endpoint (physical, virtual, container, or cloud instance) that can run processes, host files, and participate in networks.
A classification or tagging concept used to group or qualify other individuals in a particular context.

scopeNote.value: Categories are reified so they can be referenced, versioned, or scoped. They are not rigid types.

definition.value: A structured knowledge artifact capturing the evaluation, analysis, or estimation of risk, likelihood, impact, or other security-relevant attributes.

scopeNote.value: Covers risk assessments, vulnerability assessments, and impact analyses. Assessment is an Information artifact — the output of an evaluative process — not the process itself. The process producing an Assessment may be modeled as a stonework:Process or stonework:Investigation.

definition.value: An entity that has the capability and intent to conduct harmful activities within a cyber or sociotechnical context.

scopeNote.value: Parent class for stonework:ThreatActorIndividual (a single human) and stonework:ThreatActorGroup (a collective or organization). Threat actors are distinct from the threats they pose; they are the entities that carry out actions that realize threats. They may be linked to observed behaviors, techniques, targeting patterns, and strategic objectives.

definition.value: A content-centric detection rule that matches malicious activity by a specific pattern — a byte sequence, string, hash, regular expression, or network packet structure.

scopeNote.value: Includes YARA rules, Snort/Suricata rules, and AV signatures. Distinguished from broader DetectionRule subclasses (behavioral, correlation, analytic) by its tight binding to a specific known-bad indicator or artifact pattern.

definition.value: A discrete, observable instance of malicious code — a specific binary, script, or executable artifact that can be identified by cryptographic hash, file characteristics, or behavioral signature.

scopeNote.value: Represents a concrete sample rather than an abstract family concept. A single MalwareFamily may have thousands of associated samples across versions, packers, and dropper variants. Samples are linked to their family via stonework:memberOfFamily and to their file representation via stonework:hasHash or a direct stonework:File association. Properties such as stonework:drops, stonework:downloads, and stonework:communicatesWith describe the behavior of this specific sample, not the family in general.

definition.value: A calculated or assessed component used to quantify or characterize security risk, including the potential for harm and the probability of its occurrence.

scopeNote.value: Includes Risk (overall assessed exposure), Impact (magnitude of harm if realized), and Likelihood (probability of occurrence). These are analytical outputs derived from threat and vulnerability data, distinct from the conditions (SecurityCondition) that give rise to them and the countermeasures (Countermeasure) that address them.

definition.value: A state, circumstance, or disposition relevant to the security posture of a system, asset, or mission — existing independently of any measurement or assessment.

scopeNote.value: Includes Threats, Vulnerabilities, and Weaknesses. Risk, Impact, and Likelihood are assessed/calculated concepts and are modeled under stonework:RiskFactor.

definition.value: The magnitude of harm, loss, or adverse effects that would result if a threat were realized and a compromise occurred, expressed in terms of mission, business, operational, or technical consequences.

scopeNote.value: Impact represents the severity of consequences associated with a compromise. It may include effects on confidentiality, integrity, availability, safety, mission success, financial loss, or reputational damage. Impact values may be qualitative or quantitative.

comment.undefined: Instances of stonework:Impact SHOULD specify the affected asset or mission, the type of consequence, and the severity level. Impact SHOULD be represented using explicit properties rather than encoded in class IRIs or labels.

definition.value: A discrete email communication, including headers, body content, and optional attachments, transmitted over an email protocol.

scopeNote.value: Distinct from stonework:EmailAddress, which represents the sender/recipient identifier. An EmailMessage is the content artifact itself. Used to represent phishing lures, spear-phishing emails, or other email-borne threat delivery mechanisms. Corresponds to STIX EmailMessage SCO.

definition.value: A documented, structured Process that defines a sequenced set of steps, decisions, and actions to be executed in response to a specific type of event, incident, or operational need.

scopeNote.value: A Playbook provides reusable, often automated or semi-automated guidance for security operations, incident response, threat hunting, recovery, or routine tasks. It typically includes triggers, decision points, assigned roles (Agents), inputs/outputs, and success criteria.  Playbooks bridge planning and execution.

comment.en: Playbooks are often versioned, tested, and executed as instances of Process.

definition.value: A specific versioned release or build of a Product, identified by a CPE name or equivalent product identifier. Represents the unit of software actually deployed and potentially affected by vulnerabilities.

scopeNote.value: Each CPE 2.3 entry with a concrete version component maps to a stonework:VersionedProduct individual. Wildcard-version CPEs map to stonework:Product. Related to its abstract product line via stonework:versionOf.

comment.en: Instances of stonework:VersionedProduct may include operating systems, applications, libraries, devices, or embedded components at a specific release. Versioning, vendor attribution, and edition details SHOULD be represented using explicit properties rather than encoded strings.

definition.value: A specific installed instance of a VersionedProduct on a particular system or environment, as identified by a SWID tag or equivalent installation record.

scopeNote.value: stonework:ProductInstallation is the intended target for SWID tag data. The installing system, path, licensee, and configuration details belong here rather than on stonework:VersionedProduct.

comment.en: Represents the most granular product identity level: not what software exists, but where and how it is installed. Multiple ProductInstallation individuals may reference the same VersionedProduct.

definition.value: A free-text annotation attached to one or more individuals to provide additional context, analyst commentary, caveats, or confidence assessments.

scopeNote.value: Notes are analyst-authored rather than machine-generated. They may express uncertainty, sourcing context, or interpretive observations that do not fit structured properties. Corresponds to STIX 2.1 Note SDO.

definition.value: A prescribed defensive method used to detect, prevent, or respond to adversary behavior within a target environment.

scopeNote.value: Aligns with MITRE D3FEND DefensiveTechnique. Framework-specific subclasses (e.g. d3fend:DefensiveTechnique) extend this class when D3FEND data is loaded.

definition.value: A specific method by which adversaries attack AI/ML systems (e.g., training data poisoning, adversarial examples, model extraction).
Represents an Autonomous System (AS), a collection of IP routing prefixes under the control of a single administrative entity, identified by its AS number.
A structured evaluation of a specific vulnerability's applicability and risk in a particular product or deployment context.

scopeNote.value: Captures VEX-style assessments: whether a product is affected, not affected, fixed, or under investigation, together with the justification and any remediation statement. Distinct from stonework:Vulnerability (which describes the flaw itself) — a VulnerabilityAssessment is an opinion about that flaw in a specific context.

definition.value: A potential or actual source of harm arising from an adversary's capability, intent, and opportunity to exploit weaknesses or create adverse effects within a system, organization, or mission.

scopeNote.value: This class represents the abstract notion of a cyber threat, independent of specific threat actors, campaigns, or events. It provides a semantic foundation for modeling adversary capabilities, intentions, targeting, and conditions that give rise to harmful outcomes.

comment.undefined: Instances of stonework:Threat may describe adversary capabilities, strategic objectives, targeting patterns, or environmental conditions that increase the likelihood of harmful action. Threats may be linked to threat actors, campaigns, malware, TTPs, weaknesses, or assets, but are conceptually distinct from the actions or events that realize them.

definition.value: A named mutual exclusion object (mutex or semaphore) used by a process to prevent concurrent access to a shared resource. Commonly used as a malware indicator — malware families often create uniquely named mutexes to avoid re-infecting a host.

scopeNote.value: Mutex names serve as host-based indicators of compromise. A specific mutex name found on a system can be attributed to a known malware family. Corresponds to the STIX 2.1 Mutex SCO.

definition.value: An autonomous or semi-autonomous system driven by AI/ML that can act, make decisions, or be attributed responsibility in a cyber or sociotechnical context.

scopeNote.value: Covers both offensive uses (AI-assisted or autonomous threat actors) and defensive uses (AI-driven detection, response, or hunting systems). Distinct from Tool — an AIAgent has a degree of autonomous decision-making rather than being a passively invoked artifact.

definition.value: A prescribed analytical method used to process, evaluate, or reason over data to produce intelligence, detections, or assessments.

scopeNote.value: Covers structured analytic techniques (e.g., analysis of competing hypotheses, kill chain analysis, diamond model analysis) and computational analytic methods (e.g., clustering, anomaly detection). Distinct from DetectionRule — an AnalyticTechnique describes the method; a DetectionRule is a deployable artifact implementing it.

definition.value: Represents a single email address, optionally associating it with a display name and a user account.
A single cryptographic hash entry associating a hashing algorithm with its hex-encoded digest value. Used to represent entries in the STIX hashes dictionary.
A specific occurrence or performance of actions by one or more agents over time within a cyber or sociotechnical context.

scopeNote.value: One of two root classes in STONEWORK alongside CyberEntity. Superclass for Campaigns, Incidents, Operations, Events, and Processes. Aligns with BFO Occurrent and BFO Process.

definition.value: Records that a object such as an indicator, malware, tool, or threat actor was seen. Wraps observation metadata around a reference to the sighted object.
A defender-owned collection of data or information with organizational value, such as databases, intellectual property, credentials stores, or PII collections.

scopeNote.value: Represents data as a targetable resource distinct from the systems that store or process it. Used to model what adversaries seek to access, exfiltrate, or destroy rather than the infrastructure they exploit to reach it.

definition.value: An abstract malware concept representing a named strain, lineage, or campaign of malicious software sharing common behavioral patterns, code ancestry, or infrastructure. Corresponds to STIX 2.1 malware SDO with is_family=true.

scopeNote.value: Examples: Cobalt Strike, Mimikatz, WannaCry, BlackCat. A MalwareFamily does not have a specific hash or binary but may be linked to MalwareSample instances via the inverse of stonework:memberOfFamily. Use stonework:categorizedBy to assert behavioral type (e.g., stonework:Ransomware, stonework:Backdoor).

definition.value: A running or terminated process instance on a host, identified by PID, executable path, command line, parent process, and associated user account.

scopeNote.value: Represents low-level OS process objects observed during execution — distinct from stonework:Process (enterprise-level workflows). Mutex objects created by a process are linked as stonework:Mutex individuals. Corresponds to STIX 2.1 Process SCO.

definition.value: An intelligence assertion that a pattern — atomic, expression-based, or behavioral — when matched in an observed environment, indicates the presence of threat activity attributable to a specific adversary behavior, malware, or campaign.

scopeNote.value: The central concept in operational CTI. The term is used by the community in three overlapping senses, all of which stonework:Indicator covers: (1) IOC sense — an atomic observable (IP address, domain, file hash, URL) that has been assessed as malicious or suspicious and tagged for detection; in STONEWORK the underlying observable is the SCO (stonework:IPAddress, stonework:Domain, stonework:Hash), and the Indicator wraps it with the assertion, confidence, and validity window. (2) Pattern sense — a STIX patterning expression over one or more SCOs (e.g., [ipv4-addr:value = ‘198.51.100.0/24’]). (3) Behavioral sense — a multi-step or TTPs-based pattern asserting that an observed sequence of behaviors indicates a technique or campaign. Distinct from stonework:DetectionRule: an Indicator is the intelligence claim (‘look for this’); a DetectionRule is the operational artifact that implements the check (‘here is the Sigma/Snort/YARA rule that looks for it’). Indicators are produced by threat intelligence analysts and consumed by detection pipelines; DetectionRules are deployed in SIEMs, EDRs, and network sensors. Corresponds to STIX 2.1 Indicator SDO. Use stonework:indicates to link an Indicator to the AttackPattern, Malware, Campaign, or ThreatActor it asserts.

definition.value: A type of Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTP) that describes ways that adversaries attempt to compromise targets. Often maps to MITRE ATT&CK techniques.

A coordinated set of activities conducted by one or more agents toward a defined objective, typically spanning multiple campaigns, incidents, or phases and characterized by unified command, intent, or resourcing.

scopeNote.value: Operations are broader in scope than Campaigns — a single Operation may encompass multiple Campaigns executed over an extended period. Applies to both offensive operations (e.g. state-sponsored cyber operations) and defensive operations (e.g. incident response operations, threat hunting operations).

definition.value: An analyst's epistemological stance on the correctness or credibility of information asserted in another intelligence object.

scopeNote.value: Sibling to stonework:Assessment under IntelligenceProduct. Where Assessment evaluates risk or impact, Opinion evaluates the reliability or accuracy of existing intelligence — e.g., 'I disagree with this threat score' or 'I believe this indicator attribution is incorrect'. Corresponds to STIX 2.1 Opinion SDO. The opinion value (strongly-agree to strongly-disagree) and explanation are captured via stones: properties.

definition.value: A software object intended to perform malicious functions within, or on behalf of, a threat actor. Encompasses both abstract family-level concepts and concrete specimen-level artifacts.

scopeNote.value: Parent class for stonework:MalwareFamily (STIX is_family=true) and stonework:MalwareSample (STIX is_family=false). Corresponds to the STIX 2.1 malware SDO. Use stonework:categorizedBy to assert behavioral type (e.g., stonework:Ransomware). Use stonework:hasArtifact to link a sample to its captured binary.

definition.value: A time-bounded record produced by a security sensor or automated tool capturing one or more cyber observables witnessed in a monitored environment, together with frequency metadata.

scopeNote.value: Machine-produced intelligence: a sensor is not an analyst, but its output feeds the intelligence pipeline in the same way that SIGINT feeds human analysis. Key metadata: the time window the phenomenon was witnessed (first/last observed), how many times it was observed (number_observed), and which cyber observables were captured (hasObservable). Use stonework:madeBySensor to link to the producing stonework:Sensor. Distinct from stonework:Sighting, which records that a known CTI object (indicator, malware, threat actor) was seen; SecurityObservation is the raw sensor-layer record prior to attribution or indicator matching. Corresponds to STIX 2.1 observed-data SDO. Inspired by SOSA sosa:Observation — compatible in concept but does not formally import the SOSA ontology.

definition.value: A person who provides information, intelligence, or a report (as opposed to automated feeds or technical artifacts).

scopeNote.value: Often used in HUMINT or OSINT contexts. Reliability scoring is commonly applied to human sources.

definition.value: Any control, mitigation, or safeguard applied to protect against, reduce, or respond to security risks.

scopeNote.value: Includes Controls, Mitigations, CoursesOfAction, and DetectionRules. The two primary branches are preventive/reactive measures (Mitigation, CourseOfAction, Control) and detection logic (DetectionRule, Signature).

definition.value: Any entity that can act, perform actions, or be attributed responsibility in a cyber or sociotechnical context.

scopeNote.value: Covers AI, human individuals, groups, organizations, and other actors (e.g. threat actors, vendors, government bodies). Used as the top-level superclass for identity-related objects in alignment with STIX Identity.

definition.value: A sovereign state or top-level administrative entity recognized internationally.
A sub-national territorial division such as a state, province, region, or governorate.
A single human individual.

scopeNote.value: Represents real named people (e.g. employees, threat actors, researchers). Does not include legal entities or groups. Corresponds to STIX Identity with identity_class = 'individual'.

definition.value: A significant urban settlement, municipality, or metropolitan area.
Represents a user group on a system or service, including local OS groups, cloud groups, and social media groups.
Structured source references used to record the origin and trustworthiness of data and relationships.

scopeNote.value: Includes Feeds, Publications, and URL References.

definition.value: Represents a user account on a system or service, including local OS accounts, cloud accounts, and social media accounts.
Represents a network domain name. Can reference the IP addresses it resolves to.
A concrete, observable sequence of actions, commands, or behaviors that implements a technique in a specific operational context.

scopeNote.value: Procedures describe the actual steps an adversary takes, such as specific commands, scripts, tools, or configurations. They represent the most granular level of adversary behavior.

comment.undefined: Procedures are instances or patterns of execution that realize a technique. They may include command lines, API calls, malware behaviors, or operator playbook steps. Procedures are distinct from techniques, which describe generalized methods.

definition.value: A deployed system, appliance, agent, or network tap that collects data about digital artifacts, network activity, or adversary behavior for detection and investigation purposes.

scopeNote.value: Applies DetectionRules via stonework:usesRule. May be a software agent, physical appliance, virtual instance, or network sensor. Examples: IDS/IPS, SIEM collector, endpoint agent, network tap, honeypot, vulnerability scanner. An AI-driven sensor that crosses into autonomous decision-making may be additionally typed as stonework:AIAgent. Aligns with D3FEND Sensor. Inspired by SOSA sosa:Sensor — compatible in concept but does not formally import the SOSA ontology. Produces stonework:SecurityObservation instances via stonework:madeBySensor.

definition.value: An identifiable activity or sequence of activities performed over time by one or more agents to achieve an operational, security, or business objective. It transforms inputs (artifacts, data, configurations) into outputs and may be governed by plans, controls, or policies.

scopeNote.value: This class operates at the enterprise/operational level and is distinct from low-level runtime Process objects (e.g., STIX SCO Process). It is intended for modeling Controls, Playbooks, Mitigations, Threat Scenarios, and other repeatable or planned workflows.

definition.value: A reference to an external online resource (URL, article, post, etc.) used for provenance.
A deliberate action or control intended to reduce the likelihood, impact, or severity of a risk, threat, vulnerability, or adverse event.

scopeNote.value: Mitigations are proactive or reactive measures applied to address weaknesses or threats. Examples include: applying a security patch, enabling MFA, deploying a firewall rule, isolating a compromised host, or training users. A Mitigation may be a reusable control (ATT&CK sense) or a specific situational action. CourseOfAction is a subclass for contextualized, packaged response actions.

definition.value: A digital asset or wallet address used in cryptocurrency transactions, often relevant for tracking ransomware payments or illicit finance.
A specific, contextualized recommended action or set of steps to prevent or respond to a threat, attack, or incident.

scopeNote.value: More prescriptive and situational than a general Mitigation — a CourseOfAction packages guidance for a specific threat context. Corresponds to the STIX 2.1 CourseOfAction SDO. General reusable controls (e.g. ATT&CK mitigations) are modeled as Mitigation; specific incident response actions are CourseOfAction.

definition.value: A collection of threat intelligence focused on one or more topics, such as a description of a threat actor, malware, or attack technique.
Represents a geographic location. May be as specific as a latitude/longitude coordinate or as broad as a continent. At least one of region, country, or latitude/longitude must be provided.
A formal or semi-formal structured entity such as a company, government agency, non-profit, military unit, or consortium with defined boundaries and usually legal identity.

scopeNote.value: Corresponds to STIX Identity with identity_class = 'organization'. Includes corporations, government bodies, NGOs, universities, etc. Distinguished from Group by having more persistent structure, roles, and often legal standing.

definition.value: A structured digital document binding a public key to an identity, issued and signed by a certificate authority. Used for authentication, encryption, and trust establishment in networked systems.

scopeNote.value: Primarily represents X.509 certificates. May be used to cluster infrastructure sharing the same certificate or to link observed TLS/SSL artifacts to their issuing authority. Referenced by stonework:sharesCertificate on Infrastructure.

definition.value: A measure of the potential for loss or adverse effects arising from the realization of a threat, expressed as a function of the impact of compromise and the likelihood that the compromise will occur.

scopeNote.value: This class represents the assessed or estimated level of exposure to harm for a specific asset, mission, or organization. Risk is typically derived from the combination of impact and likelihood, and may incorporate assumptions, uncertainty, and contextual factors.

comment.undefined: Instances of stonework:Risk may reference the threat being considered, the assets affected, the expected impact of compromise, and the likelihood of occurrence. Risk values may be qualitative or quantitative, and SHOULD be represented using explicit properties rather than encoded in class IRIs or labels.

definition.value: Describes elements within the Windows configuration Registry system.
An analytically-defined grouping of correlated adversarial behaviors, tools, malware, infrastructure, and participants believed to share a common source or campaign thread.

scopeNote.value: Represents the intelligence analyst's working construct before enough is known to declare a Campaign: a cluster of correlated observations attributed (loosely or firmly) to a common adversary source. May evolve into a stonework:Campaign when an objective, timeline, and attribution are sufficiently established. Corresponds to the intended meaning of STIX intrusion-set — the correlated set of activity, not the actor responsible for it. Distinct from stonework:ThreatActorGroup, which is the adversary entity; a CyberActivityCluster is the attributed set of activity linked to that entity.

definition.value: Represents a Uniform Resource Identifier conforming to RFC 3986.
A technique performed within or against cyberspace, encompassing both offensive and defensive cyber operations.

scopeNote.value: Mirrors D3FEND's CyberTechnique class. Subclassed by stonework:AttackTechnique (offensive) and stonework:DefendTechnique (defensive), enabling a single property chain to span both ATT&CK and D3FEND individuals.

definition.value: A structured or semi-structured record of events, actions, or state changes generated by a system, application, or network component over time.

scopeNote.value: Logs are primary data sources for detection, investigation, and threat hunting. Examples include system event logs, authentication logs, DNS query logs, firewall logs, and application logs. Distinct from NetworkTraffic (which captures raw packet data) and from Event (which represents a parsed, security-relevant occurrence derived from log data).

definition.value: A reusable, prescribed method for achieving an objective, which may be instantiated as a concrete execution by an actor or system.

scopeNote.value: Technique is intentionally not a subclass of stones:AttackPattern. Attack patterns (e.g. CAPEC) are abstract descriptions of attack classes in the STIX sense; techniques are operationalized plans. See stonework:CyberTechnique, stonework:AttackTechnique, stonework:DefendTechnique.

comment.undefined: Mirrors D3FEND's Technique class and reflects the PROV-O Plan philosophy: a technique is a plan that describes how an action should be carried out, distinct from the activity that executes it. Subclassed by stonework:CyberTechnique for cyber-specific methods.

definition.value: A prescribed security or privacy safeguard that specifies an action, capability, or condition intended to reduce risk, enforce policy, or achieve a defined protection objective within an information system or organization.

scopeNote.value: This class provides a semantic representation of security and privacy controls from frameworks such as NIST SP 800‑53 and the CIS Controls. It supports mapping to external control identifiers and families without embedding copyrighted control text.

comment.undefined: Instances of stonework:Control may represent individual controls, control enhancements, or sub‑controls. Framework‑specific identifiers (e.g., "AC‑2", "CIS 4.1") SHOULD be modeled using explicit properties rather than encoded in the class IRI. Control text SHOULD be referenced via citations rather than reproduced verbatim.

definition.value: A behavioral or functional classification of malware, describing what the malware does rather than what it is. Corresponds to the STIX 2.1 malware-type open vocabulary.

scopeNote.value: Instances (e.g., stonework:Ransomware, stonework:Trojan) are assigned via stonework:categorizedBy. A malware object may carry multiple types. The skos:notation value gives the STIX 2.1 wire-format string for aspirational round-trip export.

definition.value: The malware type has not been determined or cannot be classified into a known category.
Software that automatically displays or downloads advertising material, often without user consent.
Malware that abuses the computational resources of an infected host, such as for cryptocurrency mining or proxying network traffic.
Malware deployed on a web server that provides remote command execution via HTTP requests, enabling persistent access through the web application layer.
A toolkit that automates exploitation of client-side vulnerabilities to deliver malware, typically via drive-by download from compromised or malicious web pages.
Malware designed to conduct or participate in distributed denial-of-service attacks against target systems or networks.
Malware that provides covert, persistent remote access to a compromised system, bypassing normal authentication.
Malware that records keystrokes on an infected system to capture credentials, sensitive data, or communications.
Self-replicating malware that spreads across networks or systems without requiring user interaction or a host file to attach to.
Malware that covertly monitors user activity, collects personal or sensitive information, and transmits it to a remote party.
Malware that infects the boot sector or master boot record to load before the operating system, enabling deep persistence and defense evasion.
Malware that replicates by inserting copies of itself into other executable files or documents, spreading when those files are executed or opened.
Malware that masquerades as legitimate security software to deceive users into paying for fake threat removal or granting elevated privileges.
Malware that encrypts or locks victim data or systems and demands payment for restoration of access.
Malware that periodically or continuously captures screenshots of the victim's display and exfiltrates them to an attacker.
Malware providing covert remote control of an infected host, typically including capabilities such as file access, screen capture, keylogging, and command execution.
Malware disguised as or bundled with legitimate software to deceive users into executing it, enabling a range of malicious payloads.
Malware designed to irreversibly destroy data or render systems inoperable, typically used for sabotage or to obscure attacker activity.
Malware that connects an infected host to a command-and-control network, enabling remote tasking as part of a botnet.
Malware whose primary function is to download and execute additional malicious payloads from a remote source.
Malware that carries and installs one or more secondary payloads onto a target system, often unpacking them from within itself.
Malware that conceals itself and other malicious software by subverting operating system or hypervisor mechanisms, typically to maintain privileged persistence.
A portable computing device with wireless connectivity, typically used for communication, data processing, and accessing networks (e.g., smartphones, tablets, or laptops with cellular capability).

scopeNote.value: In a cyber threat context, Mobile Devices are often treated as both endpoints (Infrastructure) and vectors for attacks (e.g., mobile malware, phishing, lost/stolen device risks). They may host UserAccounts, run Mobile Applications, and connect via cellular, Wi-Fi, or Bluetooth.

definition.value: An atomic label, string, or token used to uniquely identify, locate, or reference a cyber entity, resource, or principal.

scopeNote.value: Includes contact identifiers, network locators, accounts, and similar atomic artifacts.

definition.value: A structured intelligence artifact such as a blog post, advisory, report, or news article.
A captured or observed network traffic flow between source and destination endpoints, including protocol, ports, payload characteristics, and timing.

scopeNote.value: Distinct from stonework:Log (which captures parsed event records) and stonework:Event (a security-relevant occurrence). NetworkTraffic is the raw flow artifact. May carry indicators such as user-agent strings, URI patterns, or certificate fingerprints observable in transit.

definition.value: A structured list of access control entries (ACEs) that governs which principals (users, groups, or system accounts) are permitted or denied specific operations on a resource.

scopeNote.value: Applies across filesystems, operating system objects (registry keys, processes), network devices (firewall rules), cloud IAM policies, and APIs. In a CTI context, adversaries frequently modify ACLs to establish persistence, escalate privileges, or deny defenders access to compromised resources. Framework-specific extensions (e.g. Windows DACL/SACL structure) are modeled at the framework layer.

definition.value: Relates a product version to another product version it depends on.
Relates a malware sample or family to another sample or family from which it is derived, modified, or evolved — indicating shared code lineage, forked development, or deliberate repackaging.
Links a SecurityObservation to the Sensor that produced it.

scopeNote.value: Inspired by SOSA sosa:madeBySensor. Enables queries such as 'which sensor produced this observation?' and 'what has this IDS sensor observed in the last 24 hours?' The producing sensor may also be the created_by_ref identity in the STIX wire format.

definition.value: The date and time at which the vulnerability record was last modified in its source database.

scopeNote.value: Corresponds to cveMetadata.dateUpdated in CVE JSON 5.x. cve:dateUpdated is declared owl:equivalentProperty of this property.

definition.value: Links a Digital Identity to one or more atomic Identifiers that belong to it.
Relates a CyberTechnique to another related CyberTechnique via a cross-framework or cross-abstraction-level association.

scopeNote.value: Used for links such as CWE weakness → CAPEC technique (exploits/instantiates) and CAPEC technique → ATT&CK technique (operationalizes). Domain is CyberTechnique; framework-specific individuals populate the relationships at the framework mapping layer.

definition.value: Links a SecurityObservation to the cyber observable objects (SCOs) captured during the observation window.

scopeNote.value: The range covers any SCO type: stonework:IPAddress, stonework:Domain, stonework:File, stonework:NetworkTraffic, stonework:RuntimeProcess, stonework:UserAccount, etc. Corresponds to STIX observed-data object_refs. Inspired by SOSA sosa:hasResult.

definition.value: The canonical identifier assigned to this vulnerability by its originating numbering authority, e.g. 'CVE-2021-44228', 'GHSA-jfh8-c2jp-hdp9', or 'OSV-2021-1'.

scopeNote.value: Source-specific ID properties (e.g. cve:cveId) are declared rdfs:subPropertyOf this property, enabling cross-source queries on a single predicate. Each vulnerability record SHOULD carry exactly one identifier from its primary numbering authority.

definition.value: Relates an SBOM to a component VersionedProduct it inventories.
Relates a vulnerability to a structured CVSS metric record carrying the version, vector string, and base/temporal/environmental scores.

scopeNote.value: A single vulnerability may carry metrics for multiple CVSS versions (2.0, 3.1, 4.0). For a single headline score and severity, use stonework:cvssBaseScore and stonework:cvssSeverity directly on the Vulnerability. This property links to the full per-version metric objects populated by CVE ingest.

definition.value: Relates a tactic to an offensive technique that serves that tactic's goal.
Relates a hash entry to the entity it describes. The domain is a stonework:Hash individual representing a single hash algorithm and digest value.
Relates a product to another product that depends on it. Transitive to support supply chain reasoning across deep dependency trees.
Links a MalwareSample to a captured binary artifact (file, memory dump, or encoded payload) constituting the physical evidence of the sample.

scopeNote.value: Optional — a MalwareSample may be known via hashes or threat reports without the binary being available. When present, the artifact provides retrievable binary evidence. Corresponds to the STIX 2.1 sample_refs property on the malware SDO.

definition.value: The date and time at which a vulnerability identifier was assigned by the relevant numbering authority.

scopeNote.value: Corresponds to cveMetadata.dateReserved in CVE JSON 5.x. cve:dateAssigned is declared owl:equivalentProperty of this property.

definition.value: Relates a vulnerability to a product version known to be affected by it.

scopeNote.value: The range is a stonework:VersionedProduct individual whose IRI is derived deterministically from the CPE identifier. The product individual may be populated by a separate CPE ingest; references from CVE data precede that ingest and are resolved when CPE data is loaded.

definition.value: Relates a product family to the Agent (organization or person) that develops or maintains it.
Relates a threat actor group or campaign to an offensive technique they are known to employ.

scopeNote.value: Sub-property stones:uses carries the shortcut triples emitted by the STIX 2.1 transform for relationship_type 'uses'.

definition.value: Asserts that when the source Indicator's pattern is matched, it signals the presence of the target adversary behavior, malware, campaign, or threat actor.

scopeNote.value: Corresponds to STIX relationship_type 'indicates'. The domain is always stonework:Indicator. The range covers the principal threat intelligence objects an indicator can point to: AttackPattern/AttackTechnique (technique-level indicators), Malware (malware family or sample indicators), Campaign and CyberActivityCluster (campaign-attribution indicators), ThreatActor and its subclasses (actor-attribution indicators), Infrastructure (C2/hosting indicators), and Tool (tool-use indicators). A single Indicator may indicate multiple targets.

definition.value: Relates an entity to its hash entries. The range is a stonework:Hash individual representing a single hash algorithm and digest value.
Relates a vulnerability to the product version in which it was addressed.

scopeNote.value: The range is a stonework:VersionedProduct individual whose IRI is derived deterministically from the CPE identifier. Populated by CVE/patch ingest.

definition.value: The headline CVSS base score for this vulnerability, on a 0.0–10.0 scale.

scopeNote.value: When multiple CVSS versions are present, this SHOULD reflect the highest available version (CVSS 4.0 preferred over 3.1, 3.1 over 2.0). For full structured metric data across all CVSS versions use stonework:hasCvssMetric.

definition.value: Links a digital identity to the real-world Agent it is believed to belong to.
The date and time at which this vulnerability was publicly disclosed.

scopeNote.value: Corresponds to cveMetadata.datePublished in CVE JSON 5.x. cve:datePublic is declared owl:equivalentProperty of this property.

definition.value: Relates a vulnerability to the weakness class it exploits or instantiates.

scopeNote.value: The range is a stonework:Weakness individual whose IRI is derived from the CWE identifier. The weakness individual may be populated by a separate CWE ingest.

definition.value: Relates a Mitigation, CourseOfAction, or Control to the AttackPattern or Vulnerability it addresses. Corresponds to STIX relationship_type 'mitigates'.
Reference to the Markings applied by this marking entry.

Relates a vulnerability to the weakness class it instantiates or exploits. Subproperty of stonework:hasWeakness, using the directional 'exploits' semantics aligned with CVE and CWE mapping conventions.

scopeNote.value: The range is a stonework:Weakness individual whose IRI is derived from the CWE identifier. Used by cve:exploitsWeakness (rdfs:subPropertyOf this property) when CVE data is loaded.

definition.value: Relates infrastructure to the registrar, registry, or administrative authority through which the registration was processed or is maintained.
Relates a specific malware sample to the malware family it has been classified as belonging to, based on shared behavioral patterns, code similarity, infrastructure overlap, or analyst attribution.
Relates a product version to an older version it replaces. Transitive to support full product lifecycle reasoning.
Temporal succession of Information (v1 precedes v2 of a report)
Links a CyberActivity (Campaign, CyberActivityCluster, Incident, etc.) to the ThreatActor (Individual or Group) responsible for it. Corresponds to STIX relationship_type 'attributed-to'.
Shortcut triple: generic relationship. Corresponds to STIX relationship_type 'related-to'.
Relates infrastructure to the Agent recorded as its owner or registrant of record — the entity in whose name the resource is officially registered.
Shortcut triple: source STIX object is revoked and superseded by target. Corresponds to STIX relationship_type 'revoked-by'.
Relates a vulnerability to the vulnerability record that supersedes it, e.g. when a CVE is split, merged, or formally replaced by another identifier.

scopeNote.value: Corresponds to cve:replacedBy in CVE JSON 5.x, but as an object property linking to a stonework:Vulnerability individual rather than a string. The source-specific string form is preserved on cve:replacedBy.

definition.value: The qualitative CVSS severity rating corresponding to the headline base score: NONE, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, or CRITICAL.
Links a specific versioned product instance back to its abstract product family.
Relates a Sensor to the Detection Rules it applies.
Relates a product family to a specific versioned product instance.
Links any individual to one or more contextual categories.

scopeNote.value: This is the primary mechanism for flexible, context-sensitive classification (e.g., Evidence, HighValue, Suspect, etc.). Multiple categories per individual are allowed.

definition.value: Links a Technique to the Tactic(s) it achieves or supports.

scopeNote.value: This is the inverse of hasTechnique. A single Technique may support multiple Tactics (e.g. 'Phishing' supports both Initial Access and Credential Access).

definition.value: Relates an Agent to a product family it develops or maintains.
Relates a source DetectionRule, Sensor, Indicator, or defensive technique to the threat, activity, or artifact it is capable of detecting. Corresponds to STIX relationship_type 'detects'.
Shortcut triple: source targets the target Identity, Vulnerability, or Location. Corresponds to STIX relationship_type 'targets'.
Shortcut triple: source Malware or ThreatActor exploits target Vulnerability. Corresponds to STIX relationship_type 'exploits'.
Relates a specific installation instance to the versioned product it instantiates.
The CVSS vector string encoding the metric values used to compute the headline base score, e.g. 'CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H'.
Relates a weakness to the vulnerability that exploits or instantiates it.

scopeNote.value: The range is a vulnerability individual. The weakness individual (domain) is a stonework:Weakness whose IRI is derived from the CWE identifier. The weakness individual may be populated by a separate CWE ingest.
